title: 〜しか〜ない "nothing but / only (with a negative)"
meaning: "Only", with the nuance that the amount is less than expected or insufficient.
simpleExplanation: しか + negative verb means "only", with the feeling that it is not enough: 財布に百円しかない = I have only 100 yen (and that's too little). Even though the meaning is positive ("there IS 100 yen"), the verb must be negative. しか replaces が and を (野菜しか食べない) and comes after other particles (現金でしか, 先生にしか).
whenUsed: Complaining or stressing a small amount, number or range: only one person came, only cash accepted, you can only buy it here. Everyday speech and writing at all politeness levels. If you just want to state a limit without any "too little" feeling, use だけ.
formation: Noun + しか + negative: 百円しかない, 野菜しか食べない
しか replaces が / を
Other particles + しか: にしか, でしか, としか, からしか
V-dictionary + しかない = have no choice but to (歩くしかない)

diagram.title: だけ vs しか〜ない vs ばかり

examples.reading: さいふに ひゃくえんしか ない。
examples.en: I have only 100 yen in my wallet.
examples.note: Only 100 yen, and it's not enough: しか + ない.

examples.ja: 彼は野菜しか食べません。
examples.reading: かれは やさいしか たべません。
examples.note: しか replaces を: 野菜しか + 食べません.

examples.ja: この店は現金でしか払えない。
examples.reading: この みせは げんきんでしか はらえない。
examples.en: At this shop you can only pay in cash.
examples.note: で + しか: only by cash (a limitation).

examples.ja: この本は図書館でしか読めません。
examples.reading: このほんは としょかんでしか よめません。
examples.en: This book can only be read at the library.

examples.ja: 終電がもうないから、歩いて帰るしかない。
examples.reading: しゅうでんが もう ないから、あるいて かえるしかない。
examples.en: The last train has gone, so I have no choice but to walk home.
examples.note: V-dictionary + しかない = the only option.

similarGrammar.difference: だけ works with affirmative verbs and is neutral. しか always needs a negative and implies insufficiency.
ばかり = nothing but (too much). しか〜ない = only (too little).
V + しかない ("no choice but to") overlaps in meaning: 行くしかない ≈ 行かなければならない, but stresses lack of alternatives.

commonMistakes.wrong: 財布に百円しかあります。
commonMistakes.right: 財布に百円しかありません。
commonMistakes.why: しか must be followed by a negative verb even though the meaning is "only".
しか replaces を and が; it does not follow them.
Other particles come before しか: でしか, にしか.

usageNotes: しか〜ない sounds like a complaint or a limitation; だけ sounds like a plain fact.
With numbers, しか stresses fewness: 三人しか来なかった (only three came, disappointingly).
〜するしかない is a useful phrase for resignation: 諦めるしかない.
jlptTips: See しか before the blank → the verb must be negative. See a negative verb after a blank meaning "only" → しか, not だけ.
Particle order items: でしか / にしか (particle first, then しか); options like しかで are wrong.
